videos.title: Through the Digital Looking Glass
videos.tone: Excited, wondrous, inviting. Smile in the voice. Crisp energetic discovery, not shouting.

scenes.narration: What if an indicator could open a whole new perspective? Step through the digital looking glass. Meet Pivotglass: a workspace for asking better questions, following evidence, and seeing an investigation take shape.

Start with a question, an indicator, or a report. Guided coaching helps new analysts get moving. Preview local documents, choose what to admit, and open complete source details. Every step gives you something you can inspect.

Then change your perspective. Follow typed relationships. Reconstruct provenance and analyst groups. Scan the constellation for uneven coverage. A crowded case becomes a set of questions you can actually work.

Twelve evidence views reveal different sides of the same workspace: stored types, Dossier completeness, investigation and enrichment activity, connection counts, and coverage similarity. The view explains its question and exposes its exact data.

Compare competing hypotheses. Explore the investigation hierarchy. Keep likelihood separate from confidence. Structured techniques make assumptions, contradictions, and next collection needs visible. Then turn the work into a reviewable report, saved as Markdown or printed to PDF.

Choose your atmosphere, including original generative music. Begin locally with the synthetic quickstart, then enable services deliberately. Download Pivotglass from github dot com slash jarocki slash pivotglass. Follow a connection. Ask a sharper question. Discover what the evidence can show.

videos.title: Analyst Walkthrough: From Question to Handoff
videos.tone: Warm, curious, quietly wondrous and confident. Engaged teaching voice with quick conversational momentum.

scenes.narration: An investigation begins with a decision, not a verdict. In this synthetic case, we want to distinguish one operator from shared infrastructure. Pivotglass keeps the question, the evidence, and alternative explanations together. Novice coaching starts simply: What data do you have? What happened?

Do you know how it started? Here, we do not. Keep that unknown. The coach proposes questions, and the analyst edits one to ask what independent evidence would distinguish common control from shared hosting. Review before saving. Practice records participation and reflection; expertise grows through real work and feedback.

Now preview a local report. Candidate strings are separate from admitted evidence. Select the domain and long URL, then explicitly admit them with their source. The library retains the source digest. A successful preview is not admission, and a document claim is not automatically true.

Open the indicator. Read the complete value, typed relationships, original source, and collection history. The file communicates with a domain, but topology alone does not establish ownership. Keep both hypotheses. Record the conflicting explanation and what independent collection could resolve it.

Link evidence to a hypothesis with an explicit stance and rationale. The competing-hypotheses matrix lets us compare the same evidence across alternatives. Then record a structured technique run: inputs, analysis, limitations, and disposition. Required fields make the work inspectable; the analyst still evaluates the argument.

Coverage shows where the investigation has evidence and where it needs more. It does not measure danger. Likelihood asks how probable an explanation is. Confidence asks how sound and sufficient its evidence and reasoning are. Keep the collection requirement and stopping condition visible so the hunt has a purpose and a boundary.

Generate the workspace report. Review questions, alternatives, explicit evidence links, technique results, unresolved contradictions, and next steps. Save Markdown for an editable handoff, or print to PDF. Before sharing, check source handling and limitations. The next analyst should be able to reconstruct the case, challenge the judgment, and continue the work.

videos.title: PIVOT Glass: One Indicator, New Perspectives
videos.tone: Curious, energized discovery, slight suspense then delighted clarity. No ominous certainty.

scenes.narration: A file. A domain. An address. On their own, they are fragments. Pivotglass helps you follow the thread between them. This is a synthetic, offline case: the relationships are already stored, so we can explore without pretending to query a live intelligence service.

Start with invoice viewer dot bin. Its recorded relationship points to beacon check dot example. Open the domain and inspect the basis. That first pivot changes the question: what infrastructure did the file touch, and when was the connection observed?

From the domain, follow resolves to the address, then hosts to the URL. Each edge has a type. Open details at each stop instead of treating a line as proof. Now a single file has led us to an infrastructure neighborhood and a more specific collection plan.

Provenance tells you where the records came from. The chronological trail records how material entered the investigation. These are reviewable paths, not an automatically reconstructed attack chain. A missing event remains missing.

Two admitted indicators also share an analyst promotion group. The dotted edges preserve why we selected them together. That is workflow context, not evidence of one owner. Read the complete wrapped URL, filter the neighborhood, and keep the distinctions visible.

scenes.chapter: Turn a pivot into a test
scenes.narration: The useful result is a better test. Does this topology fit common control, shared hosting, or both? Record a rationale, identify independent evidence that could separate them, and choose the next authorized collection. Pivotglass turns a connection into a question you can investigate.

videos.title: Visualize, Challenge, Report
videos.tone: Bright, exploratory, accessible teacher. Wonder at changing perspectives with clear concrete delivery.

scenes.narration: The best visualization starts with an analyst question. Pivotglass offers twelve evidence views, each with a stated scope, a reason for the chart, and exact data. Let us look at the same synthetic case through several lenses.

Relationship graphs expose typed connections. Provenance history preserves admissions and analyst grouping. Connection counts identify dense neighborhoods for inspection. Graph position and node degree do not establish maliciousness or common control.

Stored-type charts summarize the inventory. Dossier completeness and the constellation expose gaps. Activity views separate investigation records from enrichment task state. Coverage similarity compares evidence profiles, not actor identity. Empty or unavailable dimensions remain visible instead of being guessed.

The competing-hypotheses matrix projects explicit support and contradiction links. Here, the same connected cluster supports both explanations. That overlap is the interesting part: it does not discriminate. Unassessed cells have no recorded stance. Open exact data to inspect rationales and mixed evidence.

A structured technique run records the method, selected inputs, findings, limitations, and disposition. In this demonstration, a key assumptions check challenges the leap from shared infrastructure to common control. Its result is an authored review and a collection need, not automatic attribution.

The hierarchy organizes questions and analytical records under the investigation. Likelihood ranges and confidence history keep probability separate from the basis for belief. Membership in a tree is organizational; it is not a support link.

Bring it together in the deterministic report: questions, hypotheses, evidence links, technique results, contradictions, and next steps. Save editable Markdown or print to PDF. Export exact chart data when a reviewer needs the underlying rows. Use the visualization to discover a question, and the report to make the reasoning reviewable.
